source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Heart rate, respiratory effort, blood pressure, temperature, and birth weight.","B":"Heart rate, respiratory effort, gestational age, birth weight, and head circumference.","C":"Heart rate, oxygen saturation, blood glucose, temperature, and muscle tone.","D":"Heart rate, respiratory effort, muscle tone, reflex irritability, and color."}}
source_row.rationale: The joint ACOG/AAP statement defines the five Apgar components as color, heart rate, reflexes or reflex irritability, muscle tone, and respiration or respiratory effort, making option D correct. Option A substitutes blood pressure, temperature, and birth weight. Option B substitutes gestational age, birth weight, and head circumference. Option C substitutes oxygen saturation, blood glucose, and temperature. Those measurements may be clinically relevant to newborn assessment but are not components of the Apgar score.
source_row.source_detail: ACOG/AAP The Apgar Score — five components: color, heart rate, reflexes/reflex irritability, muscle tone and respiration; scores reported at 1 and 5 minutes. ACOG/AAP Committee Opinion ‘The Apgar Score’ (2015 statement retained on current ACOG site); currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation; acute/complex alterations and medical emergencies. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A newborn is assigned Apgar scores at 1 minute and 5 minutes after birth. Which set lists the five components used to calculate the Apgar score?
